subject.title: resolveCliAuthEpoch invalidates every live CLI session when local credential source-of-storage flips, even though identity is unchanged

question: What should define the Claude CLI auth epoch when an OpenClaw auth profile exists and the local Claude credential source appears or disappears without proven identity change?
rationale: Current source makes storage presence part of the auth boundary, but removing it naively can keep sessions alive across a real or unprovable account change for identity-less Claude CLI OAuth profiles.

options.title: Require Proven Same Identity
options.body: Implement a Claude-specific fix that ignores local storage-source churn only when the auth/profile identity is provably unchanged, and otherwise keeps fail-closed invalidation.

options.title: Use Profile Credential As Canonical
options.body: Treat the selected auth profile as the epoch source whenever present, accepting that identity-less Claude CLI OAuth profiles may not detect some real local account switches.

options.title: Keep Fail-Closed Storage Sensitivity
options.body: Leave the current invalidation behavior in place and document/work around the credential file/keychain churn for affected users.

recommendation.title: Require Proven Same Identity
recommendation.body: Implement a Claude-specific fix that ignores local storage-source churn only when the auth/profile identity is provably unchanged, and otherwise keeps fail-closed invalidation.

likelyOwner.reason: Josh provided the most explicit maintainer-facing auth-boundary guidance on the overlapping Claude CLI auth-epoch PR.
